original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract, not another mixture already covered by the frozen catalogue.

first_step.inspect: Read the frozen catalogue bound exclusions and select one genuinely different helper endpoint inventory.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the complete optimistic child histogram and reject it immediately if even the relaxation has insufficient headroom.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Helper inventory changes can improve the moment; repacking a covered cost interface cannot evade its scoped bound.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: Apply #1240's exact relaxation to the local words of the open complex kappa claims. For each pinned claim, report its packing cap and remaining headroom.
scope_change_reason: This is the card's 'reject routes with insufficient headroom' step, applied to inventories already proposed in the review queue. No new inventory was synthesized.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. This separates packing gains from local-word gains across the queue and shows every covered claim is capped below kappa 0.0016874.
stop_rule: Cover only claims whose profile, idle histogram and live/calls are recorded together. List the rest.
evidence: RESULT.json: 14 claims, 9 words, max cap 0.0016873148; the #1148 line sits on words whose caps are 0.17-0.21% below the selected word's; 16 claims not covered.
author: Douglas Colkitt

open_questions.question: Can a W1/W2-type word be packed as tightly as the #1148 line?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the largest remaining packing prize (up to about +0.7%).
open_questions.first_step: Transplant the #1148 line's owner packing onto W1's helper widths and measure the realized fraction of the cap.
open_questions.blocked_by: The joint-entrance method changes the word; the transplant must keep W1's paid profile.

open_questions.question: Which proposals raise a cap rather than pack toward it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only those can move kappa beyond 0.0016874.
open_questions.first_step: Screen each proposal's per-call profile with ceiling.ceiling() before a full replay.
